À l'attention de la Section 4.\n\nLe cit:
For the attention of Section 4.

The undersigned citizen reports that on Sunday 9 November, after curfew, the Saint Agatha parish choir sang in the church, doors shut, by candlelight. These were not ordinary religious songs, but a gathering of defiance.

There were eleven participants, whose names I attach. The woman Ewa TILL, at the organ, was leading.

I remain a vigilant citizen.

I. KOLB

Dimanche 9 novembre, 22h30. Au cours de:
Sunday 9 November, 22h30. During the round of Saint Agatha Quay, singing was heard from the parish church, whose doors were shut and windows lit from inside.

The patrol did not go in: orders not to disturb places of worship without a warrant. The singing stopped around 23h00. Several people left by the side door.

Done and signed, Sergeant HRON.

Of the eleven names passed on, the system matched earlier occurrences:

- Four names appear in reports of religious gatherings (processions, vigils) between 1983 and 1986.
- Two names are linked to households already visited by Section 7.

System interpretation: recurring core, consistent with a network structured around the parish.

Inspecteur,\n\nUne chorale ne chante pas:
Inspector,

A choir does not sing at random on a Sunday evening: it sings for a feast day. Ask yourself which one, and whether someone had signed a paper authorising it.

The parish keeps a vigil register, and the diocese issues permits. The originals are in the archives — where I have just been sent. Ask for the Saint Agatha collection.

An informer who gives eleven names at once did not see them all. Count those who signed in.

Do not name me. K.

Two documents from the Saint Agatha collection:

VIGIL PERMIT no. 86/212, issued on 14 October 1986 by the District 2 Bureau of Religious Affairs: "Authorisation is given to the Saint Agatha parish to hold a prayer vigil on the evening of the feast of the church's dedication (9 November), beyond the usual closing hour." Signed before the curfew was tightened.

2. VIGIL REGISTER for 9 November: seven people signed in at the entrance. In the margin: "R. FALK excused (in hospital since the 3rd). J. NOWAK excused (night shift)."

KOLB, Ignác, né en 1934. Marguillier de:
KOLB, Ignác, born in 1934. Churchwarden of the Saint Agatha parish until 1985.

Applied for the post of principal organist in 1985, on the death of the former organist. The parish council preferred Mrs Ewa TILL to him. Mr KOLB left his duties the same year.

Since then, author of four reports targeting members of the parish. Three were dismissed with no further action.

Inspecteur,\n\nLes onze noms ont été tra:
Inspector,

The eleven names have been passed on. Director HALM had his conclusion before the evening bulletin, and Section 7 has its "parish network".

Eleven arrests for a Sunday evening. You will be marked down as a quick inspector.

R. MAZUR
Inspecteur,\n\nLes onze ont été interpel:
Inspector,

The eleven have been arrested. HALM is satisfied.

You had the vigil permit and the register in front of you. You knew there were seven of them, and that the vigil was authorised. You signed for the eleven all the same.

I am filing your notes. Nobody will read them. I have read them.

R. MAZUR
Inspecteur,\n\nVous avez rayé les absent:
Inspector,

You struck out the absent and the ordinary choristers, and passed on only Ewa TILL's name. The register proved you right on the number: seven, not eleven.

HALM got a name to show, which is enough for him. Section 7 would have preferred eleven. You chose the compromise: one arrest instead of eleven, but an arrest all the same.

R. MAZUR
Inspecteur,\n\nVous ne retenez qu'un nom:
Inspector,

You hold only one name, with nothing but your intuition to set against the other ten. Section 7 notes that you "lightened" a file without justifying it.

Ewa TILL has been arrested. The other ten remain on a list, somewhere.

R. MAZUR
Inspecteur,\n\nUn permis de veillée sign:
Inspector,

A vigil permit signed on 14 October, a register of seven names, an informer passed over for the organist post. You put it all in the file, and concluded with a dismissal.

HALM wanted eleven arrests before the bulletin. He got a dismissal with no further action. He asked who the inspector was. I gave him your name; I had no choice.

The Bureau of Religious Affairs will thank you in silence.

R. MAZUR
Inspecteur,\n\nVous classez un rassemble:
Inspector,

You dismiss a gathering reported by an informer and confirmed by a patrol, without producing a single document to the contrary.

The District 2 Militia heard the singing. HALM read your dismissal out loud, in a meeting. It was not a compliment.

R. MAZUR

La chorale de Sainte-Agathe a tenu une v: The Saint Agatha choir held a prayer vigil on the evening of the feast of its church's dedication, authorised by a vigil permit signed on 14 October, before the curfew was tightened. Seven people were present. The informer, Ignác KOLB, passed over for the organist post in favour of Ewa TILL in 1985, denounced eleven names out of spite, two of them absent (FALK in hospital, NOWAK at work). The ministry wants a collective example of the Saint Agatha parish.
Inspecteur,\n\nOnze noms d'un seul infor:
Inspector,

Eleven names from a single informer is a lot for a man who was watching from afar. And a choir that sings on a particular Sunday rarely sings without a reason.

The religious affairs bureau signs permits. Parishes keep registers. Those papers are kept somewhere. I will say no more.

R. MAZUR
